A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DreamCS by the same authors. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support comparison, including matching material across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original GPTEval3D experiments, MiniCPM-o evaluations, human ratings, ablation visualizations, and supplementary GA-XL results.

after.justification: v2 reports original generation experiments and human evaluations, supplemented by loss ablations, reward-model generalization tests, geometry-defect tests, and runtime measurements.

M1.justification: The reward architecture, MSE-plus-CS objective, differentiable meshization, adaptive fusion, and linear guidance ramp are retained. Appendix G.2 adds evaluated variants that apply RewardCS every two or three optimization steps instead of every step, a limited procedural extension. Newly disclosed encoder freezing does not establish an architecture change.

E1.justification: v2 adds intermediate SDS-generated meshes to training, extending coverage beyond v1's curated reconstructed assets to coarse optimization-stage geometries. Appendix D.3 adds reward-scoring evaluations on unseen noun-tag prompts and paired prompts introducing geometric defects. GPTEval3D and the existing source datasets remain represented.

E2.justification: DreamDPO expands from v1's separate four-view MVDream comparison and MVDream visualizations to v2's twelve-view DreamFusion, MVDream, and Magic3D comparisons, plus MiniCPM-o and human evaluations (Tables 1–2). Appendix D.3 also introduces comparisons of RewardCS predictions against LLaMA-Mesh reference scores.

E3.justification: Reported dataset size increases from 14,000+ to 30,000+, and the separate four-view comparison is replaced by twelve-view comparisons. New protocols include clustering indices, twenty-bin score agreement, Janus proportions, and controlled resolution/frequency timing experiments. v2 reports expanding the quality study from 30 to 60 prompts, but its Table 2 caption and Appendix F.2 retain 30, leaving the actual sample count unresolved.

E4.justification: The original t-SNE and guidance-weight visualizations are retained. v2 substantially extends analysis with quantitative separation-loss ablations at four lambda values, downstream generation ablations (Tables 4–5), unseen-prompt and geometry-defect tests, explicit Janus measurements, and resolution/guidance-frequency tradeoffs (Tables 6–7).

E5.justification: Neither version reports random seeds, repeated-training run counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. v2's ten test batches and additional study samples concern evaluation design rather than uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Retained results change: Magic3D Stage1+Reward3D GA changes from 2.86 to 2.63, and MVDream+RewardCS MiniCPM-o text alignment from 3.21 to 3.59. Changed training data and unclear GA/GA-XL continuity limit direct performance comparisons. v2 adds Janus, loss-ablation, generalization, robustness, and timing results; v1's standalone four-view and GA-XL result sets no longer appear.

T1.justification: Appendix E.1 adds mathematical definitions and equations for the differentiable renderer, SDS gradient, and forward noising. The CS-divergence assumptions, asymptotic-equivalence theorem, and proof remain unchanged across v1 Appendix A and v2 Appendix B. The explicit linear guidance equation restates v1's existing schedule.

C1.justification: The three central contributions and claims of geometric improvement and complementary 2D/3D guidance remain. The introduction enlarges the dataset contribution from 14,000+ to 30,000+ samples and states paired/unpaired equivalence without v1's explicit asymptotic qualifier, although the formal theorem remains asymptotic.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive explanations of intermediate-mesh training coverage, encoder selection and geometry/texture limitations, and the relationship between separation loss and generation quality. It interprets new scoring tests as evidence of generalization and robustness. Appendix G.2 introduces detailed computational-cost and quality-efficiency interpretations; the earlier budget and backbone limitations remain.

D1.justification: New disclosures include frozen text-encoder parameters, balanced preferred/dispreferred sampling, approximately 90 GPU-hours of reward-model training, and the default isosurface resolution of 128. Existing GPU counts, AdamW settings, 100 training epochs, and the promise of future code/model release are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for alternative surface-reconstruction methods, DeepMesh, clustering metrics, Recognize Anything, and MiniCPM. Appendix C.2 expands positioning of the mesh-construction choice. The central positioning against image-based preference supervision remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The introduction is substantially rewritten and condensed, methodology explanations expand, and the appendices are reorganized into separate LLM-use, theory, dataset, reward-model, SDS, implementation, and results sections. Ethics material moves from the former appendix, reproducibility statements are added, and citations change to author-year style.

P2.justification: v2 rebuilds the main qualitative comparison, redraws the dataset histogram, adds dataset-example panels, and expands compact qualitative composites into extensive multi-view galleries. Tables are restructured and new analysis tables added. The retained t-SNE plots move from Figure 3 to Figure 11; the guidance ablation moves from Figure 7 to Figure 6. Typography and page layout also change throughout.

improvement.justification: Tables 4–5 strengthen v1's limited evidence that CS separation improves downstream generation, while Tables 6–7 quantify previously undocumented computational tradeoffs. Expanded comparisons and geometry tests provide additional support. These benefits are tempered by inconsistent 30/60-prompt study descriptions and prose retaining values that disagree with updated tables, limiting confidence in parts of the expanded evaluation.
